findings.title: Sitemap entries mostly lack <lastmod> dates
findings.evidence: 0 of 104 sitemap URLs carry a <lastmod> value.
findings.mechanism: Crawlers use <lastmod> to decide what to re-fetch. Without it they re-crawl on their own schedule, so updated pages can be represented in answers by a stale copy for far longer than necessary.

suggested_action.summary: Emit an accurate <lastmod> for every sitemap URL.
how: Populate <lastmod> from the content's real last-modified time, not the build time.
Do not set every URL to the same timestamp on each deploy - crawlers learn to distrust it.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ACC-014 and confirm it no longer fires.

findings.title: Internal links and sitemap entries point at pages that fail to load
findings.evidence: 2 of 30 crawled URLs returned an error, e.g. https://englishtest.duolingo.com/faq (403), http://static.duolingo.com/s3/DuolingoReport_Final.pdf (fetch_error: EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker was reached).
findings.mechanism: Every dead link is a discovery path that terminates, and a visitor who reaches one usually leaves rather than navigating back. Dead entries in a sitemap additionally teach crawlers to trust the sitemap less.

suggested_action.summary: Fix or remove the broken URLs from links and from the sitemap.
how: Repair the links, or redirect the old URLs to their current equivalents with a 301.
Remove URLs that no longer exist from the sitemap.
Add a build-time link check so this does not regress.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ACC-024 and confirm it no longer fires.
